<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 11.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Executive
Compensation.<a name="Item11_ExecutiveCompensation__191339"></a></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation Discussion and Analysis <a name="CompensationDiscussionAndAnalysis_191346"></a></font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0in 0in 3.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overview of Compensation Program</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Compensation Committee (for purposes of this
analysis, the &#147;Committee&#148;) of the Board has been appointed to discharge the
Board&#146;s responsibilities relating to the compensation of the Company&#146;s
executive officers. The Committee has the overall responsibility for approving
and evaluating the Company&#146;s executive officer compensation plans, policies and
programs. The Committee&#146;s primary objectives include serving as an independent
and objective party to review these compensation plans, policies and programs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Throughout this report, the individuals who served as
the Company&#146;s chief executive officer and chief financial officer during fiscal
2006, as well as the other individuals included in the Summary Compensation
Table presented below, are sometimes referred to in this report as the &#147;named
executive officers.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0in 0in 3.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation Philosophy and Objectives</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 3.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Compensation Committee believes that a well-designed compensation program
should align the goals of the shareholders with the goals of the chief
executive officer, and that a significant part of the executive&#146;s compensation,
over the long term, should be dependent upon the value created for
shareholders. In addition, all executives should be held accountable through
their compensation for the Company&#146;s performance, and compensation levels
should also reflect the executive&#146;s individual performance during the period in
an effort to encourage increased individual contributions to the Company&#146;s
performance. The compensation philosophy, as reflected in the Company&#146;s
employment agreements with its executives, is designed to motivate executives
to focus on operating results and create long-term shareholder value by:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>establishing
a plan that attracts, retains and motivates executives through compensation
that is competitive with a peer group of other publicly-traded real estate
investment trusts, or REITs;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>linking
a portion of executives&#146; compensation to the achievement of the Trust&#146;s
business plan by using measurements of the Trust&#146;s operating results and
shareholder return; and</p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">141</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='141',FILE='C:\fc\74183331978_H11104_1874011\6776-1-eq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 15 18:34 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>building
a pay-for-performance system that encourages and rewards successful initiatives
within a team environment.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Compensation Committee
believes that each of the above factors is important when determining
compensation levels. Initially, the Committee reviews and approves annually the
chief executive officer&#146;s proposed corporate and individual performance goals
and objectives relevant to executive officers and subsequently evaluates
performance of the executive officers in light of those goals and objectives.
The Committee considers the Company&#146;s performance, relative shareholder return,
the total compensation provided to comparable officers at similarly-situated
companies, and compensation given to executive officers in prior years. To that
end, the Committee believes executive compensation packages provided by the
Company to its executive officers should include both base salaries and annual
bonus awards that reward corporate and individual performance, as well as
incentivize those executives to meet or exceed established goals.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0in 0in 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Role of Executive
Officers in Compensation Decisions</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee makes all final compensation decisions
for the Company&#146;s executive officers. The chief executive officer annually
reviews the performance of the executive officers other than himself (his
performance is reviewed solely by the Committee), and then presents his conclusions
and recommendations to the Committee with respect to base salary adjustments
and annual cash bonus award amounts. The Committee then has the ability to
exercise its own discretion in modifying any recommended adjustments or awards
to the executives (subject where relevant to applicable terms under employment
agreement), but does consider the recommendations from the chief executive
officer, as well as any self-evaluations prepared by executive officers in
light of any individual performance goals that have been pre-approved by the
Committee.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0in 0in 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Role of
Equity-Based Compensation in Compensation Analysis</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Historically, the Committee has approved only annual
base salary adjustments and cash bonus awards for executive officers, and has
not established any program pursuant to which executive officers receive
equity-based awards under the Company&#146;s Equity Incentive Plan. To date, the
only named executive officer to whom equity-based compensation has been awarded
is Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady, the Company&#146;s current chief financial officer. The grant
to Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady was part of his initial employment package under an
employment agreement that became effective on July&nbsp;1, 2006. The grant to
Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady consisted of 40,000 restricted common shares as called for by the
employment agreement, which shares will vest over a three-year period (10,000
shares upon the first anniversary of employment, and 15,000 shares for each of
the second and third anniversaries of employment).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No other equity-based
awards have been granted to executive officers or other Company employees since
inception of the Company&#146;s Equity Incentive Plan. The Committee has, however,
discussed its intention to implement a formal equity-based compensation program
for executive officers and other Company employees by the end of 2007. The
Committee views any such equity-based program as a form of long-term
compensation, and currently expects to structure the program to include the
grant of restricted common shares with vesting restrictions over one or more
years of employment. The Committee also currently plans to work with an
independent compensation consultant in structuring the terms of any such
equity-based compensation program, and to review the terms of similar programs
utilized by other peer group companies. The Committee believes that the grant
of equity-based compensation that includes a vesting period over several years
of employment will promote the Company&#146;s goal of retaining key employees, and
align the key employee&#146;s interests with those of the Company&#146;s shareholders
from a long-term perspective.</font></p>

<div>


<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Role of Employment Agreements in Determining Executive
Compensation</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each of the Company&#146;s
currently employed executive officers is a party to an employment agreement. At
the time of the Company&#146;s initial public offering in October&nbsp;2004, the
Company executed employment agreements with three of its then top executive
officers:&#160; the chief executive officer
and the presidents of the Company&#146;s student housing and military housing
divisions. Then, in July&nbsp;2006, in light of recommendations received from
independent counsel engaged by the Company&#146;s Audit Committee to conduct a
special investigation relating to accounting and auditing matters, the Company
executed employment agreements with the Company&#146;s new chief financial officer,
J. Patrick O&#146;Grady, as well as with the Company&#146;s new president of the student
housing division, John DeRiggi, and the Company&#146;s general counsel, Joseph M.
Macchione. More specifically, the recommendations from the Audit Committee&#146;s
independent counsel provided that the Committee should consider entering into
an employment agreement with its new chief financial officer, which agreement
would include severance provisions, and would reduce, compared to the Company&#146;s
past employment agreements with other executive officers, the percentage of overall
compensation linked to overall Company performance. These measures were
recommended for consideration by the Committee in an effort to ensure the chief
financial officer&#146;s independence, in light of the Company&#146;s tone-at-the-top
material weakness identified as part of the Company&#146;s evaluation of internal
control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2005. Upon
consideration of these recommendations, the Committee determined that it was
appropriate to enter into such an employment agreement with Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, the Committee
concluded that the same considerations of promoting Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady&#146;s
independence were applicable to the Company&#146;s other executive officers, and
therefore the Committee simultaneously approved of the execution of employment
agreements with the Company&#146;s other executive officers who had no such
agreement at that time. Based on the foregoing objectives, the Committee has
structured the compensation terms under these other employment agreements to
motivate executives to achieve the business objectives set by the Company and
reward the executives for achieving such objectives, as well as to promote the
Company&#146;s goal of retaining key employees.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Annual Base Salaries </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Base salaries are paid for
ongoing performance throughout the year. In order to compete for and retain
talented executives who are critical to the Company&#146;s long-term success,
the Committee has determined that the base salaries of executive officers
should be generally in line with the average of those of executives of other
equity REITs that compete with the Company for employees, investors and
business, while also taking into account the executive officer&#146;s individual
performance and tenure and the Company&#146;s performance relative to its peer
companies within the REIT sector.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each of the Company&#146;s
employment agreements is subject to an initial three-year term and provides for
the following initial annual base salaries: Gary M. Holloway,&nbsp;Sr.,
$350,000; Bruce F. Robinson, $325,000; John DeRiggi, $300,000; J. Patrick O&#146;Grady,
$300,000; and Joseph M. Macchione, $250,000. The initial base salaries included
in the Company&#146;s employment agreements for Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway and Robinson
were reviewed and recommended by The Schonbraun McCann Group LLC, an
independent consulting firm engaged prior to completion of the Company&#146;s
initial public offering in November&nbsp;2004. The initial base salaries
included in the Company&#146;s employment agreements for Messrs.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady,
DeRiggi and Macchione were evaluated by the Committee on the basis of a peer
group report compiled by the Committee&#146;s compensation consultant, which
provided an analysis of salary and bonus amounts paid to similarly-situated
employees at several comparably-sized companies. Prior to the date of
effectiveness of the employment agreements for Messrs.&nbsp;DeRiggi and
Macchione on July&nbsp;1, 2006, their annual base salaries for 2006 ($275,000
and $250,000, respectively) had been similarly evaluated by the Committee in
conjunction with its review of the independent compensation consultant&#146;s peer
group report. The Committee&#146;s compensation consultant included the following
companies as part of the Company&#146;s peer </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">143</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">group
for purposes of comparing compensation of executives: American Campus

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the

that the base salaries would be near the average of the base salaries received

(which was the initial base salary to be offered under his employment
agreement), Mr.&nbsp;DeRiggi had not yet been appointed to the position of
president of the student housing business. Once Mr.&nbsp;DeRiggi was appointed
to the position of president of the student housing business, in addition to
his current role as chief investment officer, the Committee determined that it
was appropriate to increase the initial base salary under his employment
agreement to $300,000. The base salary under Mr.&nbsp;DeRiggi&#146;s employment
agreement did not become effective until July&nbsp;1, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon the termination of
Bradley W. Harris, the Company&#146;s former chief financial officer, on March&nbsp;31,
2006, the Board appointed Dennis J. O&#146;Leary, a non-employee trustee of the
Board, as the interim chief financial officer of the Company, to serve until a
formal replacement for the position could be located. In approving the salary
to be provided to Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary during his employment by the Company, the
Committee considered that Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary was accepting the position under a
set of extremely volatile circumstances, including (i)&nbsp;the pending outcome
of the special investigation being conducted by the Audit Committee, (ii)&nbsp;anticipated
restatements to the Company&#146;s previously filed financial results, (iii)&nbsp;threats
of class action shareholder litigation, and (iv)&nbsp;the need to work with the
Company&#146;s independent auditors and the Company&#146;s forensic accountants to
complete additional procedures necessary to complete the Company&#146;s audit for
the fiscal year 2005. Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary served as the Company&#146;s interim chief

as executive vice president and principal accounting officer from July&nbsp;1,
2006 through August&nbsp;15, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Annual Incentive Bonus Awards</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the
provisions for base salaries under the terms of our employment agreements, each
executive is entitled to receive an annual cash bonus for each calendar year
during the term of the agreement, based on the achievement of&#160; individual and corporate performance goals
set by the Committee. The Committee establishes achievement thresholds for the
bonuses to be paid with respect to the achievement of these goals, as follows: (a)&nbsp;for
Mr.&nbsp;Holloway, threshold, target, superior and </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">144</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

Mr.&nbsp;Robinson, threshold, target, superior and outperformance levels equal

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the employment agreements, the
Board or the Committee is required to meet during the first 90 days of each
calendar year (120 days solely with respect to the 2006 calendar year for Messrs.&nbsp;DeRiggi,
O&#146;Grady and Macchione) to determine the relevant individual and corporate
performance goals for each executive officer for the then-current year. At the
end of that year, an assessment of individual and corporate performance against
these goals is used to determine the cash incentive bonuses to be awarded in
accordance with the following formula set forth under the employment
agreements:</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">total annual incentive bonus = <u>individual performance
bonus</u> + <u>corporate performance bonus</u></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">where:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;">individual
performance bonus</font></u></i></font> = individual performance level
achieved (threshold, target, superior or outperformance percentage, as
applicable) x individual goals allocation x base salary</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;">corporate
performance bonus</font></u></i></font> = corporate performance level
achieved (threshold, target, superior or outperformance percentage, as
applicable) x corporate goals allocation percentage x base salary</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to the
allocation of individual and corporate goals, the applicable percentages under
the employment agreements are 20% and 80%, respectively, for Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway,
Robinson and DeRiggi, and 40% and 60%, respectively, for Messrs.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady
and Macchione. In setting individual performance goals, the Committee obtains a
list of such goals from each of the executive officers, which generally include
personal objectives of the individual for the coming year that relate to their
management, and the general performance, of their respective department (or the
Company as a whole, as it relates to the chief executive officer). With respect
to corporate goals, management as a whole submits its recommendations to the
Committee as to various Company performance objectives for the coming year,
which generally are divided into goals for each of the student housing and
military housing segments, as well as the Company&#146;s overall performance on the
basis of funds from operations, or FFO. These corporate performance goals are
further broken down into threshold, target, superior or (where applicable)
outperformance levels. Historically, the corporate performance goals relating
to student housing have been based on the dollar value of student housing
acquisitions completed during a fiscal year, and goals covering military
housing have been based on the number of military housing end-state housing
units awarded under military housing privatization projects during a fiscal
year. With respect to FFO, the Committee historically has reviewed analyst
consensus for projected fiscal year FFO of the Company in setting the target
level of performance. In addition to these purely quantitative factors, the
Committee also performs a qualitative analysis with respect to the Company&#146;s
and each business segment&#146;s performance for the fiscal year. The Committee
reviews the recommendations submitted by management for both individual and
corporate performance goals, and uses its discretion in making appropriate
adjustments to the recommendations before finally approving them.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In light of the events surrounding
the special investigation performed by the Audit Committee of the Board, which
commenced in the first quarter of 2006 and did not end until the third quarter
of 2006, the Committee did not set individual and corporate performance goals
for the executive officers during the </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">145</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">respective
timeframes called for by the employment agreements in 2006. Accordingly, the
2006 cash bonus awards for executive officers, as approved by the Committee in March&nbsp;2007,
were not determined pursuant to the compensatory plan as specifically called

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In terms of evaluating the
appropriate performance levels to assign to each of the executive officers for

the second half of 2006, including his management of the engagement of a
replacement independent auditing firm for the Company and the timely filing of
the Company&#146;s Quarterly Report on Form&nbsp;10-Q for the third fiscal
quarter of 2006, which was the first timely filed filing achieved by the
Company during 2006 and was made especially challenging by the replacement of
the independent auditors during the third quarter. The Committee also noted
that Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady had been awarded 40,000 restricted common shares as part
of his initial employment package under the terms of his employment agreement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In evaluating 2006
individual performance for Messrs.&nbsp;DeRiggi and Macchione, the Committee

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to its

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equity-Based Compensation </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The employment agreements
also provide that the executives are eligible for grants of stock options and
restricted common shares under the Company&#146;s Equity Incentive Plan, pursuant to
the terms and conditions as determined by the Committee. With respect to
restricted share grants, the employment agreements provide that the shares will
have voting and dividend rights, and following the applicable restriction
period as determined by the Committee, will be fully transferable to the
executive. As stated above, the Committee has not granted any equity-based
compensation to the Company&#146;s executive officers to date, other than the
restricted common shares awarded to Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady as part of his initial
employment package. The Committee does, however, expect to implement a formal
equity-based compensation program for executive officers and other Company
employees by the end of 2007.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Perquisites and Other Personal Benefits </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s employment
agreements provide the executive officers with perquisites and other personal
benefits that the Company and the Committee believe are reasonable and
consistent with its overall compensation program to better enable the Company
to attract and retain superior employees for key positions. The Committee
periodically reviews the levels of perquisites and other personal benefits
provided to the executive officers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The executive officers are
provided the following benefits under the terms of their employment agreements:
an allotted number of paid vacation weeks; eligibility for the executive and
his spouse and dependents in all Company sponsored employee benefits plans,
including 401(k)&nbsp;plan, group health, accident, disability insurance, group
life insurance and supplemental life insurance, on such terms no less favorable
than applicable to any other executive; eligibility for participation in any
Company sponsored deferred compensation plans (of which there are currently
none that are utilized); an annual physical medical examination at the Company&#146;s
cost; a monthly car allowance; reimbursement for costs associated with tax and
financial planning assistance; coverage under a Company-paid director and
officer insurance plan on terms no less favorable than coverage provided to any
other then current officer or trustee; and, supplemental renewable long-term
disability insurance, at the Company&#146;s cost, as agreed to by the Company and
the executive. Attributed costs of the personal benefits described above for
the named executive officers for the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006,
are included in column (i)&nbsp;of the &#147;Summary Compensation Table provided
below under Item 11 of this report.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, the
executives&#146; employment agreements each contain provisions relating to payments
upon change in control events and severance upon termination for events other
than without cause or good reason (as defined under the terms of the employment
agreements). These change in control and severance terms are designed to
promote stability and continuity of senior management. Information regarding
applicable potential payments under these provisions for the named executive
officers is provided under the heading &#147;Potential Payments Upon Termination or
Change in Control&#148; presented below in Item 11 of this report.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Federal Tax Regulations</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Section&nbsp;162(m)&nbsp;of
the Code limits the deductibility on the Company&#146;s income tax return to
compensation of $1.0 million for certain executive officers unless, in general,
the compensation is paid pursuant to a plan that is performance-based,
nondiscretionary and has been approved by the Company&#146;s shareholders. The
Compensation Committee&#146;s policy with respect to Section&nbsp;162(m)&nbsp;since
the Company&#146;s initial public offering is to make reasonable efforts to ensure
that compensation is deductible to the extent permitted, while simultaneously
providing the Company&#146;s executives with appropriate rewards for their
performance.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">The
amounts in column (e)&nbsp;reflect the dollar amount recognized by the Company
as an expense for financial statement reporting purposes for the fiscal year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, in accordance with FAS 123R, with respect to
awards pursuant to the Company&#146;s Equity Incentive Plan. Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady
received 40,000 restricted shares on July&nbsp;1, 2006, in accordance with the
terms of his employment agreement that became effective as of that date. The
restricted shares vest over a three-year period, with 10,000 vesting on July&nbsp;1,
2007 and 15,000 shares vesting on each of July&nbsp;1, 2008 and July&nbsp;1,
2009. Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary, who served as the Company&#146;s interim chief financial
officer during a portion of 2006, receives grants of restricted shares for his
service as a non-employee trustee on the Company&#146;s Board of Trustees. Additional
information relating to the annual grant of restricted shares to the Company&#146;s
non-employee trustees is provided in the table below titled &#147;Trustee
Compensation.&#148;&#160; The number of restricted
shares granted to Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary for the fiscal year 2006 was pro-rated to
exclude the period of time that he served as an employee of the Company. Both
vested and unvested restricted shares receive dividend distributions made by
the Company.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Holloway&#146;s
employment agreement provides that he will receive a monthly car allowance of
$1,500, and other benefits as are commensurate with his position, including
reimbursement for the cost of tax preparation and financial planning services
up to a maximum aggregate of $10,000 annually, an annual medical examination
and six weeks of paid vacation annually and various other customary benefits.
Pursuant to Messrs.&nbsp;Robinson&#146;s and DeRiggi&#146;s employment agreements, each
will receive a monthly car allowance of $1,000 and other benefits as are
commensurate with his position, including reimbursement for the cost of tax
preparation and financial planning services up to a maximum aggregate of
$10,000 annually, an annual medical examination, five weeks of paid vacation
annually and various other customary benefits. Pursuant to Messrs.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady&#146;s
and Macchione&#146;s employment agreements, each will receive a monthly car
allowance of $650 and other benefits as are commensurate with his position,
including reimbursement for the cost of tax preparation and financial planning
services up to a maximum aggregate of $5,000 annually, an annual medical
examination, five weeks of paid vacation annually and various other customary
benefits. The employment agreements for Messrs.&nbsp;DeRiggi, O&#146;Grady and
Macchione became effective as of July&nbsp;1, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">During 2006, the
Company paid car allowances for Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway, Robinson, DeRiggi, O&#146;Grady
and Macchione of $18,000, $12,000, $9,900, $3,900 and $7,800 respectively; and
paid tax planning services for each of Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway, Robinson,
DeRiggi, O&#146;Grady and Macchione of $10,000, $10,000, $9,900, $2,500 and $7,800,
respectively. During 2006, the Trust made the following matches under the
Company&#146;s 401(k)&nbsp;plan: $1,328 (Mr.&nbsp;Holloway); $2,750 (Mr.&nbsp;Robinson);
$2,485 (Mr.&nbsp;DeRiggi); $669 (Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady); and $104 (Mr.&nbsp;Macchione);
and paid medical benefits as follows: $8,228&#160;
(Mr.&nbsp;Holloway); $8,228 (Mr.&nbsp;Robinson); $8,228 (Mr.&nbsp;DeRiggi);
$2,743 (Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady);&#160; and $2,082 (Mr.&nbsp;Macchione).
The amount shown for Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary includes $21,946 of cash fees paid in
connection with service as a non-employee trustee of the Company&#146;s Board of
Trustees.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Harris
served as the Company&#146;s chief financial officer until his termination of
employment effective March&nbsp;31, 2006. On June&nbsp;28, 2006, the Company
entered into a Confidential Settlement Agreement and General Release with
Mr.&nbsp;Harris, pursuant to which Mr.&nbsp;Harris received the right to the
following payments: (i)&nbsp;payment of $75,000, less applicable deductions and
withholdings, representing an amount equal to four months of pay at employee&#146;s
base salary as of the termination date, (ii)&nbsp;a payment of $18,750,
representing an amount equal to Mr.&nbsp;Harris&#146; bonus attributable to the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, (iii)&nbsp;a payment of $1,250, representing
payment toward outplacement service fees incurred by Mr.&nbsp;Harris,
(iv)&nbsp;commencing on August&nbsp;15, 2006, a sum of $250,000, less
applicable deductions and withholdings, to be paid in semi-monthly installments
of $9,375 in accordance with the company&#146;s normal payroll cycle, and (v)&nbsp;a
payment of $4,615 representing payment of his earned but unused vacation as of
his termination date. In addition, the Company has made a payment to
Mr.&nbsp;Harris&#146; legal counsel in the gross amount of $25,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The amounts in column (l)&nbsp;of
the foregoing table reflect the grant date fair value calculated in accordance
with FAS 123(R). During 2006, J. Patrick O&#146;Grady was the only individual to
receive a plan-based award for service as an employee. The grant was made as of
July&nbsp;1, 2006 under the Company&#146;s Equity Incentive Plan, and approved as
part of Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady&#146;s compensation pursuant to his employment agreement,
which also became effective as of July&nbsp;1, 2006. Pursuant to the terms of
his employment agreement, Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady received a grant of 40,000
restricted common shares, of which 10,000 shares will vest on July&nbsp;1, 2007
and 15,000 shares will vest on each of July&nbsp;1, 2008 and July&nbsp;1, 2009.
On July&nbsp;1, 2006, the fair market value of the Company&#146;s common shares,
based on the closing price as reported by the New York Stock Exchange, was
$13.18 per share. Under the terms of the grant, Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady will receive
dividends on all 40,000 restricted shares while he remains employed with the
Company. The Company has historically paid a dividend with respect to each of
its fiscal quarters, at a rate that is determined at the discretion of its
Board of Trustees. The restricted shares will continue to vest while Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady
remains employed with the Company, but will vest 100% immediately upon (i)&nbsp;a
change of control of the Company, (ii)&nbsp;upon the employee&#146;s termination of
employment by the Company without cause (as defined in the Equity Incentive
Plan), and (iii)&nbsp;upon the employee&#146;s death or becoming permanently
disabled (as defined in the Equity Incentive Plan). To the extent that Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady
is terminated from employment by the Company with cause, the unvested portion
of the restricted shares will be forfeited immediately to the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary received a grant of 948 restricted
shares on September&nbsp;5, 2006 in connection with his service as a
non-employee trustee of the Company&#146;s Board of Trustees. Additional information
relating to the annual grant of restricted shares to the Company&#146;s non-employee
trustees is provided in the table below titled &#147;Trustee Compensation.&#148; The
number of restricted shares granted to Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary for the fiscal year
2006 was pro-rated to exclude the period of time that he served as an employee
of the Company. Under the terms of the restricted share grant, Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary
will receive dividends on all 948 restricted shares, and the shares will vest
in equal annual installments over a three-year period (with the first
installment vesting on June&nbsp;30, 2007).</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">Represents 40,000 restricted shares granted to Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady
under the Company&#146;s Equity Incentive Plan on July&nbsp;1, 2006, pursuant to the
terms of Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady&#146;s employment agreement. The shares vest over a
three-year period, with 15,000 vesting on July&nbsp;1, 2007 and 10,000 vesting
on each of July&nbsp;1, 2008 and July&nbsp;1, 2009. Under the terms of the
grant, Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady will receive dividends on all 40,000 restricted shares
while he remains employed with the Company. The Company has historically paid a
dividend with respect to each of its fiscal quarters, at a rate that is
determined at the discretion of its Board of Trustees. The restricted shares
will continue to vest while Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady remains employed with the Company,
but will vest 100% immediately upon (i)&nbsp;a change of control of the
Company, (ii)&nbsp;upon the employee&#146;s termination of employment by the Company
without cause (as defined in the Equity Incentive Plan), and (iii)&nbsp;upon
the employee&#146;s death or becoming permanently disabled (as defined in the Equity
Incentive Plan). To the extent that Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Grady is terminated from
employment by the Company with cause, the unvested portion of the restricted
shares will be forfeited immediately to the Company. The market value of the
unvested shares is based on the closing price of the Company&#146;s common shares on
December&nbsp;29, 2006 as reported on the New York Stock Exchange, which was
$10.15 per common share.</font></p>

service as a non-employee trustee of the Company&#146;s Board of Trustees. Additional
information relating to the annual grant of restricted shares to the Company&#146;s
non-employee trustees is provided in the table below titled &#147;Trustee
Compensation.&#148;&#160;&#160; Under the terms of the
restricted share grants, Mr.&nbsp;O&#146;Leary will receive dividends on unvested
and vested shares, and the shares will vest in equal annual installments over a
three-year period. The value of the vested shares realized is calculated based
on the closing price of the Company&#146;s shares as reported on the New York Stock
Exchange on the applicable vesting date for the shares, and specifically were
as follows: with respect to a grant made on January&nbsp;1, 2005, 1,167 shares
vested on October&nbsp;28, 2005 with a value of $14.92 per share and 1,167
shares vested on October&nbsp;28, 2006 with a value of $13.88 per share; with
respect to a grant made on March&nbsp;31, 2005, 142 shares vested on March&nbsp;31,
2006 with a value of $11.64 per share; with respect to a grant made on&#160; June&nbsp;30, 2005, 120 shares vested on June&nbsp;30,
2006 with a value of $13.18 per share; and with respect to a grant made on&#160; September&nbsp;30, 2005, 227 shares vested on
September&nbsp;30, 2006 with a value of $12.62 per share.</p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change in
Control<a name="PotentialPaymentsUponTerminationO_175858"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to the Company&#146;s
employment agreements, Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway, Robinson, DeRiggi, O&#146;Grady and
Macchione, each of the executives is entitled to certain termination or
change-in-control payments. The employment agreements provide that the
executive officers agree to devote substantially all of their business time to
the performance of their duties to us under their employment agreements (except
as we otherwise agree). At the end of the initial three-year term, the
employment agreements will automatically extend for two additional one-year
periods (each, an &#147;Extension Term&#148;), unless either party terminates the
agreement by providing prior written notice to the other party not later than
60&nbsp;days prior to expiration thereof. These employment agreements permit us
to terminate the executives&#146; employment with appropriate notice for or without &#147;cause.&#148;
&#147;Cause&#148; is generally defined to mean:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>conviction
of, or the entry of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony, excluding
any felony relating to the negligent operation of a motor vehicle or a
conviction, plea of guilty or nolo contendere arising under a statutory
provision imposing per se criminal liability due to the position held by the
executive with us, provided the act or omission of the executive or officer
with respect to such matter was not taken or omitted to be taken in
contravention of any applicable policy or directive of the Board of Trustees;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>a
willful breach of the executive&#146;s duty of loyalty which is materially
detrimental to us; and</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>a
willful failure to adhere to explicitly stated duties that are consistent with
the executive&#146;s employment agreement, or the reasonable and customary
guidelines of employment or reasonable and customary corporate governance
guidelines or policies, including without limitation the business code of
ethics adopted by our Board of Trustees, or the failure to follow the lawful
directives of our Board of Trustees provided such directives are consistent
with the terms of the executive&#146;s employment agreement, which continues for a
period of 30&nbsp;days after written notice to the executive.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, each
executive has the right under his employment agreement to resign for &#147;good
reason&#148; upon certain events that occur without such executive&#146;s written
consent, provided the executive notifies us of his determination that &#147;good reason&#148;
exists within 60&nbsp;days of when the executive knows of the occurrence of the
event upon which his determination is based. For these purposes, &#147;good reason&#148;
means (i)&nbsp;any material reduction in duties, responsibilities or reporting
requirements, or the assignment of any duties, responsibilities or reporting
requirements that are inconsistent with his positions with us; (ii)&nbsp;a
reduction in his annual base salary; (iii)&nbsp;the termination or material
reduction of certain employee benefit plans, programs or material fringe
benefits other than in connection with modifications to plans that are
applicable to all similarly situated officers; (iv)&nbsp;relocation of our
offices outside of a 35-mile radius of Newtown Square, Pennsylvania; (v)&nbsp;a
failure by us to renew his employment agreement on at least comparable terms at
the close of the initial term or of either extension term; or (vi)&nbsp;our
material breach of his employment agreement which continues for a period of
30&nbsp;days after written notice. In addition, with respect to Mr.&nbsp;Holloway,
such &#147;good reason&#148; also includes his removal from the board, other than for &#147;cause,&#148;
or failure to be nominated or elected to the board, other than for &#147;cause,&#148;
absent his prior written consent.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the
event of a termination of the executive&#146;s employment by the executive or by us
(or our successor) for any reason other than &#147;cause&#148; following a change of
control, the executive will become fully vested in his options and restricted
shares and shall have a two-year period from his or her date of termination to
exercise his or her vested options. In general terms, a change of control
occurs:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>if
a person, entity or affiliated group (with certain exceptions) acquires more
than 50% of our then outstanding voting securities;</p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">155</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='155',FILE='C:\fc\74174628664_H11104_1873842\6776-1-fc.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 15 17:47 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>if
we merge into another entity, unless the holders of our voting shares
immediately prior to the merger have at least 50% of the combined voting power
of the securities in the merged entity or its parent;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>upon
the liquidation, dissolution, sale or disposition of all or substantially all
of our assets such that after that transaction the holders of our voting shares
immediately prior to the transaction own less than 50% of the voting securities
of the acquiror or its parent;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>if
our board members are elected such that a majority of the board members have
been members of the board for less than two years, unless the election or
nomination for the election of each new board member who was not a board member
at the beginning of such two year period was approved by at least two-thirds of
the board members then still in office who were board members at the beginning
of such period; or</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>if
a majority of our board votes in favor of a resolution stating that a change of
control has occurred.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway
and Robinson, if payments become due as a result of a change of control and the
excise tax imposed by Section&nbsp;4999 of the Code applies, the terms of their
employment agreements require us to gross up the executives for the amount of
this excise tax plus the amount of income and other taxes due as a result of
the gross up payment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each executive has agreed
with the Company that for a period after termination of his employment (18
months for Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway and Robinson, 24 months for Messrs.&nbsp;DeRiggi,
O&#146;Grady and Macchione), such executive will not compete with the Company by
working with or investing in, subject to certain limited exceptions noted
below, any enterprise engaged in a business substantially similar to any
primary segment of our business as conducted during the period of the executive&#146;s
employment with the Company. The executive will not be subject to these
restrictions if the Company commits a material breach of the executive&#146;s
employment agreement. In addition, these restrictions will not preclude the executive
from (i)&nbsp;making any investment in a public company or any entity in which
he is the owner of 5% or less of the issued and outstanding voting securities,
provided ownership does not result in his being obligated or required to devote
a substantial amount of managerial efforts, (ii)&nbsp;engaging in charitable,
academic or community activities, or in trade or professional organizations, or
(iii)&nbsp;holding directorships in other companies consistent with our
conflict of interest policies and corporate governance guidelines.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 14.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The employment agreements
provide that, if the executive&#146;s employment ends due to termination by us
without cause, or termination by the executive for good reason, we will be
obligated to pay the following severance benefit: (i)&nbsp;a lump sum payment
equal to (A)&nbsp;with respect to Mr.&nbsp;Holloway, three times base salary
his average annual bonus determined at the superior level of both corporate and
individual performance for the year in which the termination occurs, (B)&nbsp;with
respect to Mr.&nbsp;Robinson, two times such amount if not in connection with a
change of control and three times such amount if in connection with a change of
control, and (C)&nbsp;with respect to Messrs.&nbsp;DeRiggi, O&#146;Grady and
Macchione, two times such amount, (ii)&nbsp;a prorated amount of the incentive
bonus at the superior level for individual and corporate performance for the
year in which the termination occurs, and (iii)&nbsp;an amount equal to accrued
but unpaid base salary through the date of termination plus any other
compensation then due and owing. The Company will also permit the executive to
continue to participate in, and will pay the premiums for, group health
coverage for a period of three years following the executive&#146;s date of
termination with respect to Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway and Robinson, and two years
with respect to Messrs.&nbsp;DeRiggi, O&#146;Grady and Macchione. Additionally, all
of the options and restricted shares granted to the executive will become fully
vested, and the executive will have a period of at least two years from the
effective date of termination in which to exercise all vested options. If,
however, any executive resigns for &#147;good reason&#148; upon notice of non-renewal by
the Company after the second Extension Term, the multiplier described in clause
(i)&nbsp;above will be reduced to one times such amount. Assuming a triggering
event for these severance benefits upon </font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If an
executive&#146;s employment ends due to death or permanent disability, the Company
will pay to the executive, or his estate or beneficiary, an amount equal to one
times the executive&#146;s base salary and the executive&#146;s annual incentive bonus
(determined at the superior level for both corporate and individual performance
for the year in which the termination of employment occurs) within 10&nbsp;days
of the occurrence of the relevant event. Further, the executive will become
vested in all options and restricted shares and the executive or the
executive&#146;s personal representative will have one year from the date of the
event to exercise all vested options. The Company will pay to the executive or
the executive&#146;s representative any base salary, annual bonus, expense
reimbursement, and all other compensation related payments payable as of the
date of the relevant event. In addition, the Company will pay to the executive
or the executive&#146;s representative a prorated amount of the incentive bonus at
the target level for corporate and individual performance for the year in which
the relevant event occurred. Assuming a triggering event for these severance
benefits upon termination took place as of December&nbsp;31, 2006, the
following payments would have been due and payable to the executive officers:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the event of a termination of the executive&#146;s
employment by the executive or by us (or our successor) for any reason other
than &#147;cause&#148; following a change of control as described above, the executive
will become fully vested in his options and restricted shares and shall have a
two-year period from his or her date of termination to exercise his or her
vested options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With
respect to Messrs.&nbsp;Holloway and Robinson, if payments become due as a
result of a change of control and the excise tax imposed by Section&nbsp;4999
of the Code applies, the terms of their employment agreements will require us
to gross up the executives for the amount of this excise tax plus the amount of
income and other taxes due as a result of the gross up payment. Effective as of
July&nbsp;27, 2006, the Company entered into an amendment to its employment
agreement with Bruce F. Robinson, President of the Military Housing division.
Under the terms of the amendment, in the event of the occurrence of a change of
control (as defined in the agreement), other than a change of control resulting
from a transaction in which Gary M. Holloway,&nbsp;Sr. or Mr.&nbsp;Robinson is
a majority owner or managing member of the Company (or any successor) following
the transaction, then Mr.&nbsp;Robinson and the Company (or the buyer or
acquirer in such change of control transaction) shall enter into good faith
negotiations not later than 15&nbsp;days following the closing of such
transaction as to Mr.&nbsp;Robinson&#146;s position with, and role and compensation
in the post-closing business. If the parties to such negotiation have not
reached an agreement and have not executed an employment agreement with respect
to Mr.&nbsp;Robinson&#146;s ongoing employment after the closing not later than
30&nbsp;days following such closing, then Mr.&nbsp;Robinson shall have the right,
not later than 15&nbsp;days following the expiration of the 30-day
period, to terminate employment with the Company and have such termination
deemed to constitute &#147;good cause&#148; pursuant to the agreement; provided, however,
that such election shall not be available in the event (i)&nbsp;that
Mr.&nbsp;Robinson has become entitled to severance under any other provision of
the employment agreement prior to his termination of employment, or
(ii)&nbsp;of his death, permanent disability or the occurrence of any event
that would give the Company valid reason to terminate for cause. Assuming a
triggering event for these severance benefits upon termination took place as of
December&nbsp;31, 2006, the following payments would have been due and payable
to the executive officers:</font></p>

in the table received a grant of 1,518 restricted common shares on

fair values of the awards, also computed in accordance with FAS 123(R), with
respect to the 1,518 restricted shares granted to each of the trustees on
June&nbsp;30, 2006 was $120,042. The restricted shares all vest in three equal
installments over a three-year period. Additional information relating to the
annual grant of restricted shares to the Company&#146;s non-employee trustees is
provided in the narrative disclosure below this table. Both vested and
un-vested restricted shares receive dividend distributions made by the Company.
As of the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, each of the non-employee trustees
held the following aggregate restricted share awards: Messrs.&nbsp;Buchholz,
Kessler, Nayden , Silfen and Adm. Eastwood each held 3,665 restricted common
shares; and Mr.&nbsp;Fascitelli held 4,207 restricted common shares.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As compensation for serving on the Company&#146;s Board,
each non-employee trustee receives an annual fee of $40,000, of which $20,000
is paid in the form of restricted shares and $20,000 is paid in cash. The cash
portion of this annual fee is paid on a quarterly pro-rata basis, and the
restricted share portion of this annual fee is paid on June&nbsp;30</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font>&#160;of each fiscal year. These restricted shares
vest in three equal annual installments, are considered outstanding common
shares for purposes of voting along with our common shareholders, and receive
dividend-equivalent cash payments along with our common shareholders. In
addition, prior to 2007, non-employee trustees received $1,000 for each Board
or committee meeting attended in person and $500 for each Board or committee
meeting attended telephonically. Commencing on January&nbsp;1, 2007,
non-employee trustees will receive $1,000 for each Board or committee meeting
attended either in person or telephonically. Committee chairmen receive an
additional annual fee with the lead independent trustee receiving an additional
$5,000 per year, the Audit Committee chairman receiving an additional $7,500
per year, and the Compensation Committee chairman and the Nominating and </p>

fees were paid, and (iii)&nbsp;attendance fees for participating in meetings in
the same manner as described above for standing committees ($1,000 for
attendance in person, and $500 for attendance via telephone conference).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Trustees who also are officers or employees of the
Company receive no additional compensation as trustees. In addition, we
reimburse our trustees for their reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in
attending Board and committee meetings. Upon joining the Board of Trustees,
each non-employee trustee receives 3,500 restricted common shares that vest in
three equal annual installments. The Board of Trustees may change the
compensation of non-employee trustees in its discretion, and has delegated this
authority to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.</font></p>

Governance Guidelines. None of these trustees, or any of our executive

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 12.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Security
Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management and Related Stockholder
Matters.<a name="Item12_SecurityOwnershipOfCertain_192623"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The following table sets forth the beneficial ownership
of common shares, as of February&nbsp;15, 2007, by (i)&nbsp;each of the
Company&#146;s trustees, (ii)&nbsp;each of the Company&#146;s executive officers,
(iii)&nbsp;all of the Company&#146;s trustees and executive officers as a group and
(iv)&nbsp;any shareholders known to the Company to be the beneficial owner of
more than 5% of our common shares (based solely on information provided in Schedule&nbsp;13D
or 13G filings made by such beneficial owners with the SEC). The SEC has
defined &#147;beneficial&#148; ownership of a security to mean the possession, directly
or indirectly, of voting power and/or investment power. A shareholder is also
deemed to be, as of any date, the beneficial owner of all securities that such
shareholder has the right to acquire within 60&nbsp;days after that date
through (a)&nbsp;the exercise of any option, warrant or right, (b)&nbsp;the
conversion of a security, (c)&nbsp;the power to revoke a trust, discretionary
account or similar arrangement or (d)&nbsp;the automatic termination of a
trust, discretionary account or similar arrangement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the Company&#146;s Declaration of Trust,
shareholders generally may not have &#147;beneficial&#148; or &#147;constructive&#148; ownership
(as those terms are defined in the Declaration of Trust) of more than 7.1% of
the outstanding common shares of the Company at any time. Common shares
indicated as beneficially owned in the following table may not be deemed to be
&#147;beneficially&#148; and/or constructively&#148; owned by the shareholder under the
Declaration of Trust. The Declaration of Trust provides that the Board may
approve exceptions to this limitation of ownership, provided that the ownership
exception would not threaten the Company&#146;s ability to qualify as a real estate
investment trust under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the
&#147;Code&#148;), and currently provides the following exceptions:
(i)&nbsp;Mr.&nbsp;Holloway and persons whose share ownership would be
attributed to him under the Declaration of Trust&#146;s constructive ownership
provisions may own no more than 20% of the outstanding shares of the Company;
(ii)&nbsp;Steven Roth, the chief executive officer of Vornado Realty Trust, and
persons whose share ownership would be attributed to him under the Declaration
of Trust&#146;s constructive ownership rules&nbsp;may own no more than 8.5% of the
outstanding shares of the Company, and (iii)&nbsp;Vornado Realty, L.P., Vornado
Realty Trust, and designated affiliates or permitted transferees of Vornado
Realty, L.P. under the terms of a warrant issued by the Company, generally have
no restriction on ownership levels in the Company (except that any person who
is treated as an &#147;individual&#148; for purposes of the Code may not benefit from
this unlimited ownership exception).</font></p>

  <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:8.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">* Less
than 1%.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(1) Based
on 41,567,146 common shares outstanding as of February&nbsp;15, 2007. Under the
terms of the partnership agreement of the Company&#146;s operating partnership,
units of limited partnership interest generally may be redeemed for cash or
common shares after the units have been held for one year from the date such
units are issued (unless otherwise agreed to be redeemed earlier at the discretion
of the general partner of the operating partnership).</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(2) The
address for Gary M. Holloway is c/o GMH Communities Trust, 10 Campus Boulevard,
Newtown Square, PA 19073. The number of common shares shown as beneficially
owned by Mr.&nbsp;Holloway includes 11,550 common shares beneficially owned by
Mr.&nbsp;Holloway&#146;s wife, and includes common shares issuable upon redemption
of 16,988,829 OP units that were beneficially owned by Mr.&nbsp;Holloway as of
February&nbsp;15, 2007. Under the terms of the partnership agreement of the
Company&#146;s operating partnership, Mr.&nbsp;Holloway may require that his and his
affiliates&#146; units of limited partnership interest be redeemed for common shares
rather than cash; provided, however, that he is limited to redeeming such units

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Relates to the Company&#146;s
Equity Incentive Plan. The plan was approved in October&nbsp;2004 by the sole
shareholder of the Company prior to completion of the Company&#146;s initial public
offering. As of the date of the filing of this report, an aggregate of 43,910
restricted common shares had been granted to non-employee trustees under the
Company&#146;s Equity Incentive Plan, and 40,000 restricted common shares had been
granted to an executive officer of the Company.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 13.&nbsp;&nbsp; Certain
Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence.<a name="Item13_CertainRelationshipsAndRel_193216"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">From time to time, the Company may acquire, manage
or develop properties in which its trustees or executive officers have an
interest. The Company may recruit other persons with experience in the student
or military housing industries to join its board or management team who has
financial interests in housing properties the Company intends to acquire,
develop or manage. In transactions of this nature, there will be conflicts
between the Company&#146;s interests and the interest of the trustee or executive
officer involved, and the Company does not intend to engage in these
transactions without the approval of a majority of our independent
disinterested trustees.</font></p>

<div>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Related Party
Management and Other Services<a name="RelatedPartyManagementAndOtherSer_193228"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:6.0pt 0in .0001pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">In the ordinary course of the Company&#146;s business
operations, the Company has on-going business relationships with Gary M.
Holloway,&nbsp;Sr., entities affiliated with Mr.&nbsp;Holloway, and entities in
which Mr.&nbsp;Holloway or the Company has an equity investment. These
relationships and related transactions are summarized below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:6.0pt 0in .0001pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">In connection with the Company&#146;s initial public offering,
Mr.&nbsp;Holloway, and various entities wholly-owned by
Mr.&nbsp;Holloway, entered into a Contribution Agreement, dated
October&nbsp;18, 2004, with GMH Communities, LP, the Company&#146;s operating
partnership. Pursuant to the Contribution Agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Holloway
contributed to the operating partnership all of the partnership interests of
GMH 353 Associates, L.P., which entity&#146;s sole asset was the corporate
headquarters building located in Newtown Township, Pennsylvania. The
Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and Newtown Township each impose a 1% transfer tax
on the transfer of these partnership interests. During 2006, Mr.&nbsp;Holloway
paid the Company approximately $61,000 as reimbursement for one-half of the
aggregate transfer tax that was originally paid by the Company to the
Commonwealth and Township in connection with transfer tax assessed against the
transfer of the partnership interests. The amount paid by Mr.&nbsp;Holloway to
the Company was recorded as a reduction to corporate assets on the Company&#146;s
balance sheet as of December&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:6.0pt 0in;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Since
completion of the Company&#146;s initial public offering, the Company and certain of
its employees have continued to provide services for entities that are wholly-owned
or controlled by Mr.&nbsp;Holloway, which services include legal, IT, human
resources, payroll, accounting, marketing, and costs for office equipment and
furniture. These entities reimbursed the Company for these services provided
during the fiscal year 2006, which totaled approximately $218,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company leases space in its corporate headquarters
to entities wholly-owned by Mr.&nbsp;Holloway, including GMH Capital
Partners, LP, an entity that provides property management services for office,
retail, industrial, multi-family and corporate properties, as well as
acquisition and disposition services. During the fiscal year 2006, these
entities paid an aggregate of approximately $156,000 for the lease of space in
the Company&#146;s corporate headquarters.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is reimbursed by the joint ventures
relating to certain of its military housing projects in which the Company has
an ownership interest, as well as student housing properties under the
Company&#146;s management in which Mr.&nbsp;Holloway was an investor through
March&nbsp;2005,&#160; for the cost of certain
employees engaged in the daily operation of those military housing projects and
student housing properties. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, such
expense reimbursements relating to these military housing projects and student
housing properties totaled $64.0 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company earned
management fees amounting to $93,000 from properties in which Mr.&nbsp;Holloway
was an investor during 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&#160; Holloway
owns Bryn Mawr Abstract,&nbsp;Inc., an entity that provides title abstract
services to third party title insurance companies, from which the Company has
purchased title insurance with respect to student housing properties and
military housing projects during 2006. In connection with the Company&#146;s
purchase of title insurance for these student housing properties and projects,
the Company paid premiums to other title insurance companies, which fees in
some cases are fixed according to statute. From these premiums, the other title
companies paid to Bryn Mawr Abstract $373,000 during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2006 for the provision of title abstract services.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2005, the
Company transferred its interest in Corporate Flight Services, LLC, including
the corporate aircraft and associated debt initially contributed to the
Company&#146;s operating partnership at the time of the Company&#146;s initial public
offering, back to Mr.&nbsp;Holloway. During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, the Company paid Corporate Flight Services, LLC $993,000 for use of the
aircraft owned by Corporate Flight Services, LLC.</font></p>
